facts.raw_span: numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques over his whole body

central diabetes insipidus
growth retardation

reddish-brown papules, nodules, and plaques on his periocular areas, perioral areas, neck, shoulder, axillary folds, cubital fossa, wrists, palms, umbilical region, lateral abdomen, inguinal area, anogenital area, popliteal fossa, and ankles
Dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis consisting of histiocytes, lymphocytes, foam cells, multinucleated giant cells, eosinophils, and hemorrhage
negative for CD1a and S-100, positive for CD68

concepts.why: The presence of dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis and the positive CD68 staining are consistent with Niemann-Pick disease.
The presence of dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis and the positive CD68 staining are also consistent with Gaucher's disease.
The presence of reddish-brown papules, nodules, and plaques on the skin, particularly in the periocular and perioral areas, is consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
The presence of central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism, in combination with the skin findings, suggests a multisystem inflammatory disease.
The presence of dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis is consistent with sarcoidosis.
The presence of dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis and the positive CD68 staining are consistent with histiocytosis.
The presence of reddish-brown papules, nodules, and plaques on the skin, particularly in the periocular and perioral areas, is consistent with xanthoma disseminatum.
The presence of dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis and the positive CD68 staining are consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease.
The presence of dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis and the positive CD68 staining are consistent with Rosai-Dorfman disease.
The presence of reddish-brown papules, nodules, and plaques on the skin, particularly in the periocular and perioral areas, is consistent with juvenile xanthogranuloma.
It explains the presence of reddish-brown papules, nodules, and plaques with granulomatous infiltrate and multinucleated giant cells in the skin biopsy findings.
